title: Observability pseudonymization policy, retention automation, and immutable audit stream
creator: Asha Patel
description: Problem: Observability pipelines currently store raw identifiers and free-text which can contain customer PII (user email, phone, usernames). We need an approach that prevents accidental exposure, supports tenant-scoped retention, and provides an immutable, queryable audit stream for compliance. Goal: implement a pseudonymization-first ingest layer for traces/logs/metrics that preserves signal for debugging and SLOs while removing direct identifiers; automate retention enforcement per-tenant and per-data-class; and stream all audit events (policy changes, redaction events, privileged accesses) into an append-only audit pipeline consumable by SIEM and compliance tools.
acceptance_criteria: Ingest layer applies configurable pseudonymization rules to traces/logs without breaking trace linkage and span ids
Retention engine can enforce per-tenant retention windows and perform secure deletion or irreversible truncation of KV fields
RBAC checks applied at ingest ensure only allowed service accounts can opt-out of redaction (requires explicit approval)
Immutable audit stream implemented as append-only Kafka topic with encryption-at-rest and HMACed offsets, accessible to compliance team via read-only consumer
E2E test coverage demonstrating unchanged latency percentiles (p50/p95) within acceptable thresholds after pseudonymization applied
Documentation and runbook created for incident response and data subject access requests (DSARs)
tasks: Design pseudonymization spec (hashing vs tokenization vs format-preserving pseudonymization) and map to data classes
Implement ingest filter for traces that replaces user-identifying fields with deterministic salted tokens
Add per-route redaction policy config in Console and expose via policy API
Build retention worker that marks records for secure deletion and runs irreversible truncation jobs
Create append-only audit stream topic with ACLs and encryption and wire into SIEM playbook
Performance test pipelines with replay corpus and measure overhead
Write docs, PRs, and training for support and compliance teams
decision_log: 2026-02-26: Chosen deterministic HMAC-based pseudonymization over tokenization because it preserves joins across services without requiring a central token service
2026-03-03: Agreed to keep span/trace ids unchanged; only replace user-facing tags and attributes to preserve debugging signal

2026-03-06: Opted for append-only audit stream (Kafka topic with immutable retention and HMACed offsets) rather than storing audit events in primary observability DB to reduce risk of accidental mutation
2026-03-08: Decided on per-tenant retention policy enforced by ephemeral storage marker that triggers scheduled irreversible truncation jobs rather than synchronous deletion at ingest

telemetry_implementation_notes: Implement HMAC_SHA256 with tenant-scoped salt stored in KMS. Use deterministic pseudonymization for fields: user.email, user_id, account_name, and any attribute flagged by pattern-matching rules. Preserve length/format for downstream parsers by substituting hex-encoded HMAC truncated to 16 bytes. Add header X-Redwood-Pseudo-Version to traces to indicate transform version.
rollout_plan: Stage 0: Unit and integration tests; perf bench with 24h replay corpus (team: eng-observability)
Stage 1: Canary ingest in eu-west-1 for 2 tenants (non-prod) for 72 hours; validate dashboards and SLOs
Stage 2: Gradual ramp to 30% of production; monitor latency/error dashboards and DSAR queue
Stage 3: Full roll out for all hosted tenants; schedule retention truncation jobs during maintenance window
Stage 4: Offer enterprise customers migration guide for Dedicated/Private with optional tokenization gateway
mitigations: Fallback route: allow routing to unmodified pipeline for authorized debugging sessions subject to audit and time-limited expiry
Implement sampling-based raw retention for short window (48h) for safety while ensuring it is strictly access controlled
Alerting on HMAC key access anomalies and sudden increases in DSAR requests
audit_consumer_integration: Provide read-only Kafka consumer group for Compliance with exported schemas in Schema Registry
Ship CloudWatch/Kafka metrics for audit-topic lag, consumer throughput, and HMAC verification failures
Create a Grafana dashboard for audit-topic health and policy-change events
notes: This ticket differs from previous telemetry redaction work by emphasizing pseudonymization with deterministic joins and an immutable audit stream. Coordinate with PM (Sofia Chen) for default policy knobs and with Security for KMS/HSM key lifecycle. Expect follow-ups: DSAR automation, DSAR UI for tenants, and Dedicated-hosted migration docs.
